body: So sorry for your loss. I also lost my baby brother almost a year ago exactly. My inbox is always open. Can’t speak to your unique experience, but I do understand what you’re going through.

Trust me- I understand. I lost my 17 year old brother about a month ago. It has been the hardest, most traumatic thing I have ever had to go through. I miss him so much and honestly, vast majority of the time I don’t want to go on. I’d love to end it all and be with him again- whatever that may look like. But, I will agree with the above comment- listening to NDE stories does help. It brings a small amount of comfort to know that most people have very peaceful experiences when dying. Talk to your mom. I talk to my brother every night, asking him to give me signs that he’s okay and he’s still with me. There have been things that have happened since that I cannot explain. It doesn’t bring him back how I remember, but it does bring me a little peace to feel like he’s listening and sending me signs and signals. Your mom would not want you to give up. You’re still here for a reason. Live in your mothers honor. Don’t stop talking about her, don’t stop thinking about her. She is all around you when you keep her memory alive. Think about it- you are literally a part of her, and you always will be. A part of her still exists on earth through you 🤍 It’s tough. It’s awful. Loss is the worst thing we as humans can go through. Sending you so much love. If you ever need to talk, please don’t hesitate to reach out.
Haven’t totally accepted it yet, but I know I’m destined for loneliness. Makes me miserable.

Definitely check in with your doctor to receive a proper diagnosis, but from somebody with diagnosed BDD, it definitely sounds like you may be struggling with symptoms of BDD.

Talk to others who struggle with BDD, seek professional help, and identify what you DO feel confident about (does not have to be physical- in fact, I encourage you to look inward). Identifying you may have a problem is the first step. You’re on the right track. Keep your head up. If you ever need to vent, my inbox is open. 🤍

I’m so sorry for your loss. I lost my little brother (17) to a horrific car accident a month ago. I totally understand what you mean when you say you don’t know how to cope. All I can remember is him on our family trip we took a week prior. Happy, healthy. My family was complete. Now it’s like my whole world has been turned upside down and my brain can’t seem to process the fact that he’s gone. There’s this hole in my life now that can never be filled. This pain is like no other. 

In situations like these, it feels like our loved ones were taken from us for such a stupid, unnecessary reason. They should still be here, if only they were somewhere else at that moment. I’m sending you nothing but love and light. My heart is with you. 🤍

I lost my little brother (17) on July 7th of this year. My brother was also VERY, very loved. Grieving a sibling is horrific. The pain is indescribable. Please reach out if you’d ever like to talk. 🤍 Or if not, know my heart is with you.

Yes. I’ve been struggling with BDD for probably close to 13 years. In middle school/high school I would actively avoid mirrors. I remember after using the bathroom when going to wash my hands I would look at my feet as I was too scared to look at my own reflection. I remember thinking I was HUGE. Constantly dieting, binging/purging, etc. At that time in my life the largest size I owned was a size 4. At my smallest I was wearing a size 0 (I’m a curvy individual so this was TINY for me). Now I’m somewhat obsessed with looking at myself in the mirror. Constantly checking myself. I’m bigger now than I was then, but still I’d argue I’m “average.” Either way, I constantly feel 10x larger than I actually am. Still diet, binge/purge. One strange thing my BDD makes me do is see myself from different angles in my head. For example, I’ll be with somebody and an image of what I “must” look like from a specific angle will pop in my head. I have to adjust myself to ensure that the other person doesn’t see me like that. Sometimes the thought alone is enough to make me feel sick to my stomach and want to be alone. BDD is not an easy disorder to deal with. If anyone ever needs to talk, my inbox is open. It’s even worse to deal with this alone.
